Subject: Sudden p95 latency and 502 spike on our private VPC

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency increase (from ~220ms to >1.2s) and a surge of 502s on our private VPC deployment starting ~08:45 ET. This is affecting our triage and claim ingestion pipeline.

Attached: server_logs_1113.zip, grafana_shot_1113.png

Key points:
- Error rate: 502s rose from 0.2% to ~6% in 30 mins
- Inference throughput dropped ~35% while CPU on nodes is 60% (no obvious saturation)
- Spike correlated with nightly batch window but started outside expected window

We need urgent help — can you confirm Redwood has visibility into the private nodes and propose immediate mitigations? Shield's customers are impacted and we may need an incident call.

Thanks,

Anika —

Thanks for the alert and the artifacts. I'm pulling the customer-facing logs now and triggering an ops triage. We do have telemetry from the private control plane (VM/K8s + node exporter) and the beaconed inference metrics — I can confirm we see the same p95 bump and 502s on our side.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether the nightly batch started early or if any maintenance jobs ran near 08:30 ET?
- If you can share any recent deploy tags (agent/operator) that would help.

Short mitigation I'm proposing before the call: enable the fallback model (model-v1-fallback) for the affected route and reduce concurrency to 60% for 30 mins to stabilize the queue. If you approve, we'll make the change and monitor.

I'll get Tessa and Marissa on a quick triage and loop Rishi for exec visibility. Proposing a 09:40 ET call — does that work?

- Logan

Date: 2026-11-13T09:33:00-05:00
Subject: Shield Health — immediate triage (private VPC p95/5xx)

Team — bringing you up to speed. Shield Health private cluster (cluster-123) is experiencing a sudden p95 jump to >1.2s and 502s (~6%). Customer reports throughput down ~35% and attached logs indicate repeated decoder timeouts. They observed the start ~08:45 ET.

What I have checked: control-plane heartbeats ok, no node restarts on our side, model processes running. Initial traces show increased time in the decode stage and repeated KV cache misses on long prefixes.

Ask:
- Tessa: can you take the lead on a quick kernel/decoder trace and check whether any recent kernel changes or quantized runtime paths were rolled for this customer?
- Marissa: please validate autoscaler behavior for the reserved pool (did it refuse to scale due to quota or pinned capacity?)
- Laura: prep a short exec note if this escalates beyond our standard SLA window (Shield is priority enterprise).
- Rishi: pinging you for potential SLA credit and board-level awareness if mitigation >2 hours.

Attaching: triage_notes_1113.md (I'll populate with findings). We should converge on a proposed mitigation within 20 minutes.

— Logan
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Anika Sharma <anika@shieldhealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:58:00-05:00
Subject: Shield Health — triage update and temporary mitigations

Anika / team — quick update from triage (summary attached).

Findings:
- Decoder thread p95 and tail latency spiked; stack traces point to a small subset of requests hitting a longer context path that forces repeated KV cache population and a heavy attention kernel for these prefixes.
- KV cache eviction rate for the model's shard increased by ~8x at 08:44 ET. This aligns with a concurrent internal batch job doing long-context indexing that we didn't expect to overlap.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes because reserved pool was pinned; nodes reported ~60% CPU but very high wait on the decoder (~30% io/wait-equivalent).

Immediate mitigations applied (09:50 ET):
- Reduced concurrency for the impacted model route to 55%.
- Enabled model-v1-fallback for the route to a slightly lower-latency variant (no functional regression observed in quick smoke).
- Increased KV cache retention on the shard as emergency config (manual override) to avoid immediate thrash.

Effect: p95 down from >1.2s to ~420ms, 502s dropping toward baseline but still elevated (~1.1%). Throughput recovering but not yet back to normal. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps:
- We'll run a deeper decode kernel profile to confirm whether a patch is needed for the attention kernel path.
- Recommend scheduling a brief maintenance window to run the nightly indexing outside the hot path or reserve additional burst nodes for that window.

Attachment: triage_notes_1113.md (summary + quick traces).

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

We should prepare a one-page executive summary for Shield's CTO and our Customer Success lead — Laura, can you coordinate? Marissa, please prepare the cost estimate for the SRE support and the credit.
